questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: No options for on-campus housing. You will be randomly assigned to the appropriate dormitory. Typically, it will be a shared room, perhaps with one or two roommates.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Daily meals are provided by the student canteen, and students can also choose to prepare simple meals in the dormitory. Hong Kong's food delivery business is also very developed, you can choose to book on the app.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: In CUHK, the dormitories are usually halfway up the hill, and the usual way is to take the campus bus. It is relatively difficult to ride a bicycle because the road slope is very steep. So if you go out a lot, it might be inconvenient. In addition, there are no night buses on campus, meaning that at night (such as 11pm or later) you can only walk or take a taxi back to your dormitory.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The situation for undergraduate students and postgraduate students are different, this comment is only for the registration for postgraduate students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
For postgraduate students, your first step will be an online pre-selection, which usually starts before other degree students, but the number and range of options are very limited. It's hard to enroll in your favorite graduate course at this stage.
After the official start of semester, they will enter add/drop week, and exchange students are not allowed to choose courses through the system during this stage. You are always required to submit your application directly to the course provider by email. You need to download the application form from the website yourself, edit it and send it to the appropriate department for approval. If approved, you will receive a stamped document. You will also need to submit it by yourself to the department responsible for exchange student affairs (i.e. OAL).
The process of negotiating with the course provider is very cumbersome, and it is difficult to get any guarantees up front. You need to be patient at this stage. It is important to note that if you really want to register for a course, you must maintain attendance at this stage, even if you do not have formal registration permission. Many professors will not waive your absence just because you have not yet secured a place in the class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: OAL is always available to help, including an in-person tutorial. They will know your pre-selected courses in advance and confirm their registration status. In addition, they will find out about other courses that you are not pre-selected for, but would like to try to register for during the add/drop week. They will tell you which college or department you need to apply to. However, the final decision is in the hands of the course provider, and OAL cannot provide any guarantee.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Pre-selection stage: I applied for six courses and five of them have been registered successfully.
Add/drop phase: I dropped four of the pre-selected courses. I applied for about 12 new courses and four of them have been registered successfully.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Quotas for postgraduate courses are always very limited, and they usually give priority to ensuring enrollment of degree students. Once you have confirmed that you want to register for a certain course, you should apply to the course provider as soon as possible. In many cases, course registration will be on first-come, first-served basis.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If you are a postgraduate students, you should only take the 5xxx or 6xxx courses in CUHK. KU's Academic Affairs department will review your courses list in pre-approval to see if it meets the requirements for a postgraduate program. If there are any questions, you should speak with KU's academic supervisor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: CUHK courses have a faster teaching pace and more course content. The number of Assignments is also much more than that of KU. In the Hong Kong teaching environment, the academic content will be more cutting-edge. During the course, you will experience more lectures, but the professor will provide fewer opportunities for discussion. You do more face-to-face discussions with professors after class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: OAL regularly hosts activities for exchange students, and they provide many opportunities for foreigners to learn about Hong Kong and Chinese culture. Sports activities rely on a number of sports associations, and students can actively send applications. There are also many unofficial organizations in exchange students' social media groups that regularly organize games.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exchange students to keep an eye on their email. All extra-curricular activities will be sent via email.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: During some traditional Chinese festivals, you can also try to explore some folk activities on your own, please always pay attention to the news and social media.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me as Chinese people, it is easy for me to adjust to the local culture. English is not always worked in any place. Always get your translator prepared.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You can choose to participate in the exchange activities offered by OAL or get in touch with foreign students who have previously studied at CUHK. Whatsapp and Wechat will be the main communication tools.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hong Kong uses more cash or a transportation card they call Octopus, which you can use in almost any restaurant or mall. In some big shopping malls, credit cards or alipay/wechat pay will also work.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cantonese Culture, Chinese Culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient in your course selection, pay attention to safety (such as typhoons), and learn as much Chinese (Cantonese or Manderin) as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
